transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Li, Evan Rivera (Redwood); Priya Rao, Liam O'Connor, Rachel Kim, Devon Park (Pacifica)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Hand-off from AE to CSM/SE. Pilot scope: 6-week pilot for checkout assistant and store insights, emphasize <=150ms p95 for short queries, data to remain in us-west region, SOC2 plus customer-managed keys preferred.

--- Topics ---
00:00 Speaker: Maya Patel (Redwood AE) - Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, AE hand-off to our customer success and SE. We'll run through the kickoff, confirm the pilot scope, and then Jordan will walk through the runbook. Evan will cover technical deep dive follow-ups.
00:22 Speaker: Priya Rao (Pacifica CTO) - Hi Maya, hi all, thanks. Short intro from our side: I'm Priya, we run infra and platform. Liam's our DevOps lead, Rachel is PM owning the checkout assistant use case, Devon is our security lead.
00:36 Speaker: Rachel Kim (Pacifica PM) - Hi team. Quick context: main success metric is accuracy of intent detection and sub-150ms latency for snippet classification on 95th percentile. We're aiming to reduce support deflection by 20% in Q4.
00:50 Speaker: Jordan Li (Redwood CSM) - Great. Just to confirm timeline: initial pilot start in two weeks, six week pilot. Is that still accurate on your end?
01:05 Speaker: Priya - Prefer to start asap, two weeks is tight but doable if network and sample data are ready. We also need a security review before we exchange any PII-ish examples.
01:20 Speaker: Devon Park (Pacifica Security) - Yeah, we'll scrub PII but we need to see Redwood's SOC2 docs and KMS flow. We prefer customer-managed keys if possible, or a clear KMS integration pattern.
01:33 Speaker: Maya - Totally, we'll share SOC2 and our KMS integration notes. Important to call out options: hosted API (fastest), dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and private VPC option. Evan, do you want to high-level the differences?
01:45 Speaker: Evan Rivera (Redwood SE) - Sure. Hosted is quickest — no infra changes, tokens billed on usage. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can pin model versions. VPC and on-prem are for when you need network isolation or on-prem data residency; for VPC we do peering and you can bring your own KMS via our private deployment flow. Also note continuous batching and KV cache behaviors that affect latency/cost.
02:15 Speaker: Liam - Quick question, when you say KV cache, are you referring to key-value cache for chat? I think our team misheard K V cash sometimes in docs.
02:26 Speaker: Evan - Yes, KV cache — it stores attention cache to speed up consecutive tokens, reduces cost for chat-like workloads. Sorry about the audio transcripts sometimes turning it into K V cash.
02:40 Speaker: Priya - On constraints: our production SLOs are tight. For checkout assistant we need 99th p50-ish? sorry, typo — p95 150ms is ideal, p99 under 500ms maybe acceptable. We need benchmarks in our region (us-west-2).
02:58 Speaker: Maya - Understood. For pilot we'll run a small benchmark with your sample queries to measure p50/p95/p99 and compare hosted vs dedicated variants. Jordan will coordinate benchmarks.
03:12 Speaker: Jordan - I'll own that. I'll need a sample traffic dump or representative query set plus expected qps. Also, what's the expected concurrency?
03:28 Speaker: Rachel - For pilot, start with 20 qps steady, bursts to 100 qps during promotions. Long term we'll scale but pilot is small.
03:40 Speaker: Liam - On networking, we prefer VPC peering for staging. Can Redwood support private endpoints? We don't want traffic traversing the public internet for sensitive payloads.
03:53 Speaker: Evan - Yes, we support VPC peering for private deployments; for hosted we can enable private endpoints and IP allowlists. There is a bit of work to exchange CIDRs and firewall rules.
04:07 Speaker: Devon - Also, SSO: we need to provision RBAC so our analysts have read-only access to dashboards. Support SAML SSO?
04:17 Speaker: Maya - Yes, SAML SSO supported; we'll share SSO guide. RBAC is available — we can map groups to roles.
04:28 Speaker: Priya - Data residency: all stored logs must stay in us-west and retention configurable. Is that in the console?
04:38 Speaker: Jordan - Console has retention settings; we can set retention windows, and for private deployments you control where logs live. For hosted we'll store logs in-region and can provide deletion runbooks.
04:52 Speaker: Priya - Good. One of our concerns from procurement is vendor lock and exit plan. How do we export data at the end of pilot?
05:05 Speaker: Evan - We provide export APIs and can run data dumps, also we publish the schema for stored artifacts. We'll detail the exit plan in the runbook.
05:18 Speaker: Rachel - Pricing question — ballpark for pilot to estimate cost: if we run 6 weeks at avg 20 qps, what are the main levers?
05:32 Speaker: Maya - Primary levers are model choice, batching settings, and whether you use dedicated or hosted. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching suggestions that can reduce token cost. I'll send the pricing worksheet.
05:46 Speaker: Priya - Can you share an example pricing snapshot? We want to compare to AcmeAI which quoted something lower but we're wary about their latency claims.
05:58 Speaker: Maya - We'll include a comparison note; we try to be transparent with unit economics so you can model cost per 1k tokens and expected monthly spend.
06:12 Speaker: Devon - Security again: KMS. We need to know if you support customer-managed keys, HSM, and if key rotation affects availability.
06:25 Speaker: Evan - We integrate with AWS KMS; customer-managed keys are supported in the VPC/private flow. Rotation is handled without downtime — we'll include the architecture diagram.
06:39 Speaker: Liam - Network ports — do you require outbound HTTPS only? We'll open egress to certain endpoints?
06:49 Speaker: Evan - Yes, typically HTTPS to our endpoints; for VPC peering it's internal. We'll send the CIDR ranges and hostname list.
07:03 Speaker: Jordan - Okay moving to runbook steps: 1) Exchange legal and security docs; 2) Provide sample dataset; 3) Staging access & SSO; 4) Run bench; 5) Review results and decide on dedicated vs hosted.
07:18 Speaker: Priya - That order works. From legal side, we'll need a data processing addendum before sample data. Who's the contact for contracts?
07:29 Speaker: Maya - I'll loop in our contracts team, but I can share the template NDA/DPA.
07:38 Speaker: Rachel - For sign-off criteria: 1) p95 latency <150ms for classification; 2) accuracy above current baseline by 5 points; 3) acceptable cost per 1k tokens. Does that sound reasonable?
07:53 Speaker: Evan - Yes, we'll help set up metrics and alerting in Redwood Console so you can track tokens, latency, and quality.
08:04 Speaker: Priya - One worry: for the checkout assistant we might need deterministic outputs for certain flows. Can we do function/tool calling or structured output?
08:16 Speaker: Evan - We support structured output and function calling. For deterministic pieces we recommend using a smaller tuned model or reranking pipeline to ensure consistency.
08:30 Speaker: Liam - On the dedicated capacity, how quickly can you provision GPUs? If pilot looks good we may want to reserve capacity quickly.
08:41 Speaker: Maya - Provisioning depends on region and capacity; typical lead time is a few days to a couple weeks. We can discuss reserving burst capacity as an interim step.
08:55 Speaker: Devon - Audit logs: can we get token-level logs and who accessed which prompts? We need that for compliance.
09:06 Speaker: Jordan - Yes, audit logs are available. We can provide token-level breakdowns and also tie actions to SSO identities. Retention subject to plan.
09:18 Speaker: Priya - A quick note on benchmarking: please include cold-starts and warm runs in the results, because our traffic has a lot of short lived sessions.
09:29 Speaker: Evan - Absolutely — we'll run synthetic loads reflecting both patterns.
09:36 Speaker: Rachel - Any gotchas we should know for the sample dataset format?
09:42 Speaker: Evan - JSONL with fields for prompt, expected response and metadata is best. Avoid PII; if needed use tokenized or masked examples.
09:52 Speaker: Priya - Ok we'll sanitize and send by next Wednesday.
10:00 Speaker: Maya - I'll recap the immediate owners: Maya will send runbook and pricing; Evan will schedule and lead the SE deep dive; Jordan will coordinate benchmarks; Priya/Liam will share dataset and network info; Devon will request SOC2/KMS docs.
10:18 Speaker: Devon - I'll also need to confirm whether Redwood uses any third party telemetry or analytics that might send logs offsite. We need full list of subprocessors.
10:30 Speaker: Jordan - We'll include subprocessors in the security pack.
10:35 Speaker: Priya - One more: how do you handle model rollouts and version pinning if we train or fine-tune?
10:45 Speaker: Evan - We support model version pinning and can roll back. For fine-tuning we recommend a staging channel and can do canary traffic split.
10:56 Speaker: Rachel - Great. Any integration with our event bus? We use Kafka for ingestion.
11:04 Speaker: Evan - We have connectors and can ingest via Kafka or HTTP. For real-time low-latency flows we usually recommend direct API calls from the service that needs inference.
11:17 Speaker: Liam - For staging, we'll want a service account and key rotation policies. Is there a recommended rotation cadence?
11:26 Speaker: Jordan - We recommend rotation every 30/60 days depending on your policy. We support short-lived tokens for automation.
11:36 Speaker: Maya - All right, looks like we're aligned. Any blockers from Pacifica side to start the pilot in two weeks?
11:44 Speaker: Priya - Only if legal and dataset exchange are delayed. We'll try to push those.
11:51 Speaker: Devon - Security review might take a week; we'll prioritize.
11:58 Speaker: Maya - Perfect. Final recap and next steps: we'll send runbook and pricing EOD 9/11, Evan will send SE deep dive Doodle for week of 9/15, customer to send sanitized dataset and CIDR lists by 9/15, Devon to request SOC2 docs by 9/14.
12:16 Speaker: Rachel - Thanks everyone, excited to get started.
12:21 Speaker: Priya - Thanks, talk soon.
12:24 Speaker: Maya - Thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcript had occasional name swaps and punctuation missing; speakers sometimes labeled generically. Some technical terms were mistranscribed in the raw auto-txt (eg KV cache -> K V cash), corrected in notes above.
